CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging by the judgment dated 31.07.2020 passed by MACT,
Srirangapatna in MVC No.1620/2017.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 13.10.2017 when the claimant was proceeding on goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA- 09-C-8391 on Mysore-Bangalore road,
near VRL office, Mysore, at that time, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-09-F- NC: 2024:KHC:32429 5072.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondents appeared through counsel and filed written statements denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The claimant, in order to prove the case, examined himself as PW-1, and Dr.Girish Chandra.R was examined as PW-2, and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P29.

On behalf of the respondents, three witnesses were examined as RWs-1 to 3 and got exhibited NC:
2024:KHC:32429 documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R6.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal Anilkumar B R vs Mahesh B T on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129459099/
2 further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.10,13,140/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the owner of the offending vehicle to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
LIABILITY:
a) The claimant was working as an employee under respondent No.1 as cleaner-cum-loader in the vehicle, which belongs to respondent No.1.

On 13.10.2017,
when the claimant was traveling in the goods vehicle bearing KA-09-C-8391, he has sustained injuries due to the negligence of the driver of the said vehicle.

The owner of NC: 2024:KHC:32429 the said vehicle has appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement and in his evidence, he has admitted that the claimant was working under him as a cleaner.
Under the circumstances, the Tribunal has erred in holding that the claimant was traveling in the goods vehicle as a gratuitous passenger.
This finding of the Tribunal is contrary to the materials available on record.
b) The owner of the offending vehicle has paid extra premium.
Hence, the claimant is entitled for compensation under the MV Act and the Insurance Company is liable to pay entire compensation.

QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
a) Firstly, the claimant asserts that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by working as cleaner.
However, the Tribunal has erred in taking the income as merely as Rs.7,000/- per month.
b) Secondly, the claimant has examined the doctor as PW-2.

The Tribunal undervalued the claimant's whole-body disability at 19%, contradicting the evidence of the doctor NC: 2024:KHC:32429 that the claimant suffered 56% permanent disability to the spinal chord.
c) Lastly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 52 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:
LIABILITY:
The seating capacity of the offending vehicle is 1+1.
But, the driver along with two persons were traveling in NC: 2024:KHC:32429 the offending vehicle.
The claimant was traveling as a gratuitous passenger.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on the owner of the offending vehicle.
QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION a)

Firstly, the assertion of claimant that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month,
remains unsubstantiated due to lack of documentary evidence.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant notionally.
b) Secondly, the Tribunal considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and evidence of the doctor, has rightly assessed the whole body disability at 19%.

c) Thirdly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and considering the age and avocation of the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are just and reasonable and it does not warrant interference.
NC: 2024:KHC:32429 d) Lastly, in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Venkateshan.V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount appears excessive.

With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.
8.
The learned counsel for the owner of the offending vehicle has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle has appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement.
In the evidence, the owner has admitted that the claimant is an employee working as a cleaner under him.
He contended that even though the policy is taken under the Workmen Compensation Act, he has paid the extra premium and the policy taken is a package policy.
Hence, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the entire compensation.

In support of his contention, he has relied NC: 2024:KHC:32429 upon the decision of the Apex Court in the case of RAMCHANDRA -V- REGIONAL MANAGER, UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED reported in 2013 5 Supreme 696 and judgment of this Court in MFA No.3005/2009 disposed of on 27.11.2018.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and original records.

10.

The specific case of the claimant is that on 13.10.2017 when the claimant was proceeding in goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-09-C-8391 as a cleaner, working under respondent No.1 (owner of the goods vehicle), on Mysore-Bangalore road, near VRL office, Mysore, at that time, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-09-F- 5072.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32429 sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
After recovering from injuries, the claimant has filed the claim petition seeking compensation.
11. Respondent No.1 has appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement and in the evidence, he has admitted that the claimant is an employee working under him since past 3 years.
He has also admitted that when the claimant was traveling in goods vehicle belonging to respondent No.1, he has sustained injury.
The policy has been marked as Ex.R-2.
As per Ex.R-2, it is a package policy and extra premium has been paid by the owner of the offending vehicle 12.

The Apex Court in the case of Ramchandra (supra) in paragraphs 16, 17 and 18 has observed as follows:
16.

The learned Judges therefore held that in case the owner of the vehicle wants the liability of the insurance company in respect of death of or bodily injury to any such employee as is described in clauses (a) or (b) or (c) of proviso (i) to Section 147 (1)
(b), the same should not be restricted to that under the Workmen's Compensation Act but should be more or unlimited, but he must take such a policy by making payment of extra premium and the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:32429 policy should also contain a clause to that effect.

entities.text: clauses (a) or (b) or (c) of proviso (i) to Section 147 (1)
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: However, where the policy mentions "a policy for Act Liability" or "Act Liability", the liability of the insurance company qua the employees as aforesaid would not be unlimited but would be limited to that arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act.

The learned Judges were, therefore, pleased to hold that the liability of the insurance company to satisfy the award would be restricted to that arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act and the owner of the vehicle was held liable to satisfy the remaining portion of the award.

Anilkumar B R vs Mahesh B T on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129459099/
5 17.

sentences.text: A perusal of the aforesaid judgment and order of this Court thus indicate that this Court has clearly held that the liability to pay compensation in respect of death or bodily injury to an employee should not be restricted to that under the Workmen's Compensation Act but should be more or unlimited.
However, the determination would depend whether a policy has been taken by the vehicle owner by making payment of extra premium and whether the policy also contains a clause to that effect.

18. Thus in so far as the view of the High Court is concerned to the extent that the compensation would be restricted to be paid only to the extent which is payable under the Workmen's Compensation Act by making a sweeping generalisation, the same is clearly contrary to the view taken by this Court even in the judgment and order on which reliance has been placed by the counsel for the respondent-insurance company as it is sufficiently clear and unambiguously laid down which is recorded hereinbefore that the compensation payable to the employee cannot be restricted merely under the Workmen's Compensation Act and it can be expanded provided the contractual document which is the policy of insurance incorporates such clause regarding the premium to be paid taking into account the nature of the policy.
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:32429 13.

Relying on the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Ramchandra (supra), this Court in a similar case in MFA 3005/2009 disposed of on 27.11.2018, in paragraphs 7, 8 and 13 has held as follows:
7.

On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for respondent-Insurance Company contended that Ex.D1 policy clearly discloses that premium is paid only in respect of the driver and no premium is paid in respect of the cleaner.
The other contention of the appellant that it comes under non- fair passenger and collection of Rs.75/- does not come to the aid of the appellant.
In the absence of payment of definite premium in respect of the cleaner, the liability cannot be fastened on the Insurance Company other than the liability under the Workmens' Compensation Act.

The Tribunal while considering the matter on merit has considered the conditions and the details mentioned in the policy and held that though it is mentioned as package policy it did not cover the risk of a cleaner as contended by the appellant that the proviso of IMT 39 deals with legal liability to persons employed in connection with the operation and/or maintaining and/or loading and/or unloading of motor vehicles.

it is the contention of the respondent-Insurance Company that the provisions of IMT 39 is not applicable to the case on hand and no specific premium is collected in respect of the cleaner and from a reading of provisions of IMT 39 it is clear that it is in respect of personal injury to any paid driver(or cleaner or conductor or person employed in loading/or unloading but in any case not exceeding seven in number including driver and cleaner) and the premium paid for non-fair passenger is not applicable to the case on band.

Hence, the Tribunal has rightly discussed in detail relying on the decisions and has rightly come to the Anilkumar B R vs Mahesh B T on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129459099/
6 - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:32429 conclusion that the Insurance Company is liable only under the Workmens'
Compensation Act.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In reply, the counsel for the appellant contended that IMT 39 is specific with regard to legal liability to persons employed in connection with the operation and/or maintaining and/or Loading and/or Unloading of Motor Vehicles and it also includes any paid driver(or cleaner or conductor or person employed in loading/or unloading but in any case not exceeding seven in number including driver and cleaner).
Hence, the policy covers the cleaner also.
14. In view of the decisions referred above, it is very clear that the Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the owner.
Accordingly, the finding of the Tribunal in respect of liability is concerned, the same is modified.
It is held that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the entire compensation to the claimant.
15. Further, the finding of the Tribunal that the claimant was traveling as a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle, is contrary to the materials available on record.
Hence, the said finding of the Tribunal is set aside.

QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
16.
The claimant claims that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any documents to - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:32429 substantiate his claim.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income has to be assessed.

According to the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for accidents occurred in the year 2017, notional income shall be taken at Rs.11,000/-
p.m.
17.
As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained open wound on left leg with deformity and tenderness and restriction of movement.
The doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant has suffered permanent disability of 56% to spinal chord.
Therefore, taking into consideration the deposition of the doctor and injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, the Tribunal has rightly taken the whole body disability at 19%.
The claimant is aged about 26 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
Thus, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.426,360/- (Rs.11,000*12*17*19%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
The nature of injuries indicates that the claimant must have been under rest and treatment for a period of 3 months.

Consequently, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.33,000/-
Anilkumar B R vs Mahesh B T on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129459099/
7 (Rs.11,000*3 months) under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. The claimant was hospitalized as an inpatient for more than 52 days in the hospital and subsequently received further treatment.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also undergone surgery.

Considering the prolonged pain during treatment as well as the permanent disability certified by the doctor, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and sufferings' from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.50,000/- and under the head of 'loss of amenities' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
20 . Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:
